circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, which has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding those established in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track that loops around a lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and holds FIA Grade 1 status. It serves as the permanent venue for the Australian Grand Prix and hosts various supporting racing categories throughout the year.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally constructed as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following extensive modifications and rebranding as the A1-Ring, the track resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, positioned along the waterfront boulevard, spanning 6. 003 kilometers to rank as the fourth-longest Formula One venue. The circuit debuted with the 2016 European Grand Prix before hosting the Azerbaijan Grand Prix annually from 2017 onward.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and has hosted the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, marking the championship's inaugural Middle Eastern race. The venue holds a FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates various motorsport categories including drag racing, GP2 Series, and endurance competitions, with multiple track configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer Spanish circuit combines extended straightaways with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and features spectator facilities accommodating approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated near Spa in Belgium's Wallonia region, this 7. 004 km circuit has been hosting the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1925 and participated in the sport's inaugural season in 1950. The venue has maintained an annual Grand Prix presence from 1985 onward, with only 2003 and 2006 absent from its racing calendar.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361-kilometre circuit hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix annually. Beyond F1, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sports car championships and North American open-wheel and stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit is a Chinese motorsport venue located in Jiading that gained prominence as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. In addition to hosting the Formula One race, the facility began staging the Shanghai ePrix, an electric racing championship, from 2024 onward.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue located near villages in Northamptonshire that has served as the permanent home of Britain's Formula One Grand Prix since 1987. The track gained historical significance by hosting the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, having previously staged the British Grand Prix from 1948 onwards. Beyond Formula One, the circuit also accommodates the British MotoGP round annually.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the inaugural Formula One venue held east of the Iron Curtain when it hosted its first Grand Prix in 1986, commemorating Hungarian motorcycling pioneer János Drapál. Built in just eight months outside the city near a major highway, this 4. 381 km circuit was constructed faster than any other Formula One track, after initial plans for a street layout in Budapest's central park were abandoned by the Hungarian government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The Italian Grand Prix has been held there nearly every year since 1949, making it one of the longest-serving Formula One venues, and its reputation as "the Temple of Speed" stems from its characteristically long straights and fast corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue managed by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture that regularly hosts Formula One and Super Formula racing competitions. With a spectator capacity of 155,000, it stands as one of the sport's most prominent racing facilities.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its concentration of major hotels and casinos. The track passes by several iconic venues including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, weaving through the heart of one of the world's most recognizable entertainment districts.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Mexico City's 4. 3 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honors two fatal racing drivers, the Rodríguez brothers, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 on its current configuration after a 23-year absence, with the race rebranded as the Mexico City Grand Prix from 2021 onward.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Purpose-designed by Apex Circuit Design, the track joined the Formula One calendar in 2022 and primarily hosts the Miami Grand Prix, though Formula E has adopted a modified version of the circuit beginning in the 2025–26 season.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches 3. 337 kilometres through Monte Carlo and La Condamine, utilising the city's streets alongside Monaco's harbour as its racing surface. The track is frequently known by the name "Monte Carlo," reflecting that the majority of its layout occupies the Monte Carlo district of the principality.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit features steeply banked corners and dramatic elevation swings that earned it the nickname "The Rollercoaster in the Dunes. " The venue hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until the partnership concluded in 2026, with its high-speed turns like Tarzan and Hugenholtz creating one of Formula One's most distinctive racing experiences.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits north of Doha in Qatar and stretches 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, a 4. 309 km circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal plane crash eight years earlier. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features additional karting facilities honoring fellow racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront. Since 2021, it has served as the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix and began hosting an electric racing championship event in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay district, incorporating sections of both the Downtown Core and Kallang planning zones in a street-based racing configuration.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometres and features a balanced combination of extended straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for drivers across multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 facility that regularly hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix along with several other major motorsport series including NASCAR and MotoGP. Beyond its current racing calendar, the track has previously served as a venue for various championships spanning IndyCar, sports car racing, and rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand on the international stage.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he claimed back-to-back world titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while collecting 32 race victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso achieved notable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, claiming two Le Mans 24 Hours titles with Toyota, and capturing the Daytona 24 Hours in 2019, making him the sole driver to win both the Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured eight race victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto is a Brazilian racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Audi.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas has secured two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while representing Mercedes during 2019 and 2020. Currently competing for Cadillac, Bottas has accumulated 10 race victories throughout his 13-season Formula One career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with Alpine, bringing his driving talents to the international championship series.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian motorsport competitor, holds a reserve role with Haas while pursuing his racing ambitions in the European Le Mans Series, where he drives in the LMP2 category for Nielsen Racing. He has appeared at seven Formula One events across the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French driver currently racing for Alpine in Formula One, having previously achieved a career-defining victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: French-Algerian driver Isack Alexandre Hadjar races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple career records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One and has achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, including a Le Mans 24 Hours victory with Porsche in 2015.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One for the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver, competes for Ferrari in Formula One and has secured nine race victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while driving for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: K-Mag is a Danish driver competing in endurance racing for BMW's WRT team and part-time in NASCAR with Trackhouse Racing. He previously raced in Formula One across two separate stints, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship title. Over his eight-season career, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. Earlier in his career, he secured a Grand Prix victory in 2021 while driving for Alpine at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican motorsport competitor, currently drives for Cadillac in Formula One. The 15-season veteran finished second in the championship standings during 2023 while with Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver competing for McLaren who has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One over a 14-season span from 2011 through 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured eight grand prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Carlos Sainz Jr. , a Spanish driver, currently races for Williams in Formula One after competing in the sport for 12 seasons, during which he has secured four Grand Prix victories.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who contested Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to other racing series. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously raced in IMSA's LMP2 division with Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently competing for Aston Martin in the championship.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese racing driver currently functioning as a reserve driver for Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls. He competed as a full-time Formula One driver from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen is a Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing who has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. The 73-time Grand Prix winner has established himself as a dominant force across his 12 seasons in Formula One.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole representative in Formula One competition, raced in the series from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He holds the distinction of being the only driver from his nation to have participated in the sport's top category.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Based at Enstone, this team operated as Renault's factory effort in Formula One, competing under the Alpine banner from 2021 onwards following a rebranding to showcase the luxury sports car division. The squad maintained its works team status throughout Renault's involvement in the sport, which concluded at the conclusion of the 2025 season.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has entered Formula One multiple times throughout its history, with the current iteration operating under AMR GP Limited and competing as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing operations of the Italian luxury marque and stands as both the longest-tenured and most accomplished outfit in Formula One history, participating continuously in the championship since its inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially referred to by their emblem's equestrian moniker, maintains an unbroken presence across seven decades of grand prix racing.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR team proprietor Gene Haas debuted in the 2016 championship season. Leadership transitioned from Guenther Steiner, who guided the squad from its 2014 establishment through early 2024, to Ayao Komatsu as the new team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering firm, established by Peter Sauber in 1970, initially made sports cars before transitioning to Formula One machinery as an independent manufacturer. The operation achieved notable success in endurance competition, including a Le Mans victory in 1989, before competing in the championship from 1993 until its departure in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-serving constructors. Audi acquired the team and its operations in 2024 to serve as the foundation for its own Formula One entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship arrangements. The squad operates as part of the wider McLaren Group, with ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954, operating both as a constructor and engine supplier. The current iteration, Mercedes-AMG Petronas, is headquartered in Brackley and competes under a German license, with ownership shared among the Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff from 2022 onwards. The squad is traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows" due to its iconic silver livery.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor established in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned entries alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team competes as Red Bull's second constructor in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as part of Red Bull's multi-team ownership structure alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with additional facilities near Milton Keynes, the team operates as a second constructor within the Austrian conglomerate's racing programme.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operated under an Austrian licence from its English base, emerged in 2005 as a Formula One competitor and has become one of two Red Bull GmbH-affiliated teams in the sport. Christian Horner led the team from its inception through 2024, with Laurent Mekies assuming the leadership role thereafter.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering Limited, a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the dissolution of Williams's prior racing venture, has competed continuously in the sport. Based at their Grove, Oxfordshire facility, the team competes in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team.
